svg.title: Movement disorders with normal power: a cerebellar lesion lets movement start but makes it inaccurate, on the same side, with the subdivision deciding the signs; a basal ganglia imbalance either blocks starting (Parkinson disease, hypokinetic) or releases unwanted movement (chorea, hyperkinetic); each column gives the signs and the circuit that failed

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: Abnormal movement, power NORMAL: cerebellum or basal ganglia?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: both are SIDE LOOPS: cortex → loop → thalamus → cortex

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: no upper motor neurons of their own, so NOT an upper motor neuron disorder

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: CEREBELLUM: movement starts, but is INACCURATE

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: signs on the SAME side as the lesion

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: BASAL GANGLIA: release vs suppress is off

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: dopamine: direct pathway UP, indirect DOWN
